Rashi on Pesachim 54a:10:1.english: In the east [mikedem] - [Created] prior to the world.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:10:2.english: Of old - Before the world [was created].

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:10:3.english: Tofteh - For whoever is enticed [mitpateh] by his [evil] inclination falls there.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:11:1.hebrew: מרום מראשון - מרום הוא בערבות. מראשון — מקודם העולם, וכן מקום מקדשנו נברא מראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:11:1.english: On high from the beginning - It is on high in Aravot. "From the beginning" [means] before the world, and likewise, "the place of our Sanctuary" was created from the beginning.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:12:1.hebrew: חללה - חלל של גיהנם קודם בריית העולם, ותירוצא הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:12:1.english: Its void - The void of Gehenna [was created] before the creation of the world, and [this] is an answer.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:13:1.english: It has no eternal extinguishing - For it is the fire of Gehenna.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:13:2.hebrew: חזר וכללו - לקרותו טוב, לפי שהרשעים נידונין בו:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:13:2.english: He later included it - to call it good, because the wicked are judged in it.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:14:1.hebrew: אלא - ודאי אור דגיהנם נברא בשני בשבת, והא דתניא לעיל "אור בערב שבת" — באור דידן. ודתניא ברישא במו"ש — לא תיקשי: כאן במחשבה, כאן ביצירה; בערב שבת עלה במחשבה ליבראות, ולא נברא עד מוצאי שבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:14:1.english: Rather - Certainly the fire of Gehenna was created on the second [day] of the week. And that which was taught above, [that] fire [was created] on Shabbat eve, [refers] to our fire. And [as for] that which was taught in the first [baraita, that it was created] at the conclusion of Shabbat — there is no difficulty: here [it refers] to [God's] thought, [and] here [it refers] to [actual] creation; on Shabbat eve it arose in [God's] thought to be created, and it was not [actually] created until the conclusion of Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:14:2.english: And he ground [them] - He pressed, struck, and rubbed one against the other.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:15:2.hebrew: פסול היה - שאחיו מאמו היה אביו, כדמפרש שבא צבעון על אמו והוליד:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:15:2.english: He was unfit - For his maternal brother was his father, as [the Gemara] explains, that Zibeon cohabited with his mother and fathered [him].

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:15:3.hebrew: אלה בני שעיר וגו' - וצבעון וענה, אלמא אחי הוו. וכתיב: אלה בני צבעון ואיה וענה, אלמא בנו היה:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:15:3.english: These are the sons of Seir, etc. - "and Zibeon and Anah" — thus, they were brothers; and it is written, "These are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah" — thus, [Anah] was [Zibeon's] son.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:16:1.hebrew: שמואל קרי ליה רבא שבור מלכא, משום דבקי היה בדינין והלכתא כוותיה בדיני, כדין היוצא מפי המלך שמתקיים. ושבור ממלך פרסיים היה בימי רבא:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:16:1.english: Rava called Shmuel "King Shapur" because he was expert in [civil] laws and the halakhah follows him in [civil] laws, like a decree that issues from the mouth of the king, which is upheld. And Shapur was a king of the Persians in the days of Rava.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:1:1.hebrew: ואיש תבונה ידלנה - הבין מה היה בלבו של עולא, שהיה מסתכל בו:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:1:1.english: And a man of understanding will draw it out - [Rabba bar bar Chana] understood what was in the heart of Ulla, who was looking at him.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:1:2.hebrew: זה עולא - שהבין מדבריו של רבה בר בר חנה טעות, וחזא ביה בישות, וסתם דבריו שלא אמר לו כלום. והיינו "עצה בלב איש", דנקיט ליה בלביה ולא אמר לו: למה אמרת כך:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:1:2.english: That is Ulla - For he understood an error from the words of Rabbah bar bar Chanah, and saw something wrong in it, and concealed his words, in that he said nothing to him. And that is [the meaning of] "counsel in the heart of man," that he kept it in his heart and did not say to him, "Why did you say this?"

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:1:3.english: And in accordance with whose [opinion] do they hold - Ulla and Rabbah, who did not want to concede to the words of Rabbi Abba.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:1:4.english: The people act - [That is, they] follow [this] practice.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:3:1.hebrew: באור ששבת - שהיה בשבת, שדלק היום, ומכל מקום ממלאכת עבירה שבת — שדלק בהיתר, כגון של חיה ושל חולה, או נר הדולק מערב יום הכפורים — מברכין אף במוצאי יום הכפורים, דההיא ברכה משום דדבר חידוש הוא לו, שלא נהנה מן האור היום:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:3:1.english: With fire that rested - That was at rest [on Yom Kippur] — [meaning] that it burned that day, yet nevertheless rested from forbidden labor, as it burned permissibly, such as [a lamp] for a woman in childbirth or for a sick person, or a lamp that was burning since the eve of Yom Kippur — we recite the blessing [over it] even at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, because that blessing is due to the fact that it is something novel for him, since he did not benefit from the light during the day.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:3:2.hebrew: באור היוצא מהעצים - דנברא עכשיו, אין מברכין עליו במוצאי יוה"כ אלא במוצאי שבת, שאף הוא תחילת בריית אור:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:3:2.english: With fire that emerges from wood - Which was created now: one does not recite a blessing over it at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, rather [only] at the conclusion of Shabbat, for it too is the beginning of the creation of fire.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:5:1.hebrew: רבי מפזרן - רבי כשראה אור מברך עליו מיד, וכשמביאין לו בשמים לסוף שעה מברך עליהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:5:1.english: Rabbi distributes them - When Rabbi saw light, he would recite a blessing over it immediately, and when they brought him spices after a while, he would recite a blessing over them.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:5:2.english: Collects them - Over the cup [of wine], as we do.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:6:1.hebrew: באר - בארה של מרים, סלע שיצאו ממנו המים על ידי משה. ועגול כמין כברה היה, ומתגלגל עמהן כל מקום שהולכין:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:6:1.english: A well - [This is] Miriam's well, a rock from which the water came out through Moses. And it was round like a kind of sieve, and rolled along with them wherever they went.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:6:2.english: Writing - The naming of the letters.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:6:3.hebrew: המכתב - חקיקתן וצורתן, כך שמעתי. ולי נראה: כתב זו היא חקיקת צורתן, והמכתב הוא עט וחרט שנכתב בו חקיקת הלוחות, כי ההיא דקדושין (דף כא:): מניין לרבות הסול והסירא והמכתב? ונראין דברי, דקרייה לא קרי ליה כתב:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:6:3.english: The writing instrument [hamikhtav] - Their engraving and their form; so I have heard. But to me it seems [that] ketav is the engraving of their form, and hamikhtav is a pen and stylus with which the engraving of the tablets was written, like that [teaching] of Kiddushin (fol. 21b): “From where [do we derive] to include the sharp thorn [sol], the thorn [sira], and the stylus [mikhtav]?” And my words appear [correct], for in naming it, one does not call it ketav.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:6:4.hebrew: ומערה שעמד בו משה - ושמתיך בנקרת הצור עד עברי (שמות ל״ג:כ״ב). וכן באליהו: וילך עד הר האלהים חורב, ויבא שם אל המערה וילן שם (מלכים א י״ט:ח׳-ט׳):
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:6:4.english: And the cave in which Moses stood - "And I will put you in a cleft of the rock until I pass by" (Exodus 33:22). And similarly regarding Elijah: "And he went to the mountain of God, Horeb, and he came there to the cave and lodged there" (I Kings 19:8-9).

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:6:5.english: To swallow the wicked - The congregation of Korach.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:1.hebrew: והפרד - אין כל חדש תחת השמש, ופרד ראשון נברא מן הארץ ולא בא מן הכלאים:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:1.english: And the mule - There is nothing new under the sun, and the first mule was created from the earth and did not come from crossbreeding.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:3.hebrew: השמיר - כמין תולעת היה, ואין כל דבר קשה עומד בפניו שלא יתפרק. ובו בנה שלמה את הבית, במסכת גיטין (דף סח.):
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:3.english: The shamir - It was a kind of worm, and no hard object could stand before it without splitting apart. And with it Solomon built the Temple, [as stated] in Tractate Gittin (68a).

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:4.english: The tongs - [In Old French,] tenailles [tongs] of iron.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:6.hebrew: בצבתא מתעביד - על ידי צבת אחרת היא עשויה, שאוחזה בצבת ומכה בקורנס עד שנעשית, וצבתא קמייתא מאן עבדא:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:6.english: Is made with tongs - It is made by means of other tongs, for one holds it with tongs and strikes [it] with a hammer until it is made; and who made the first tongs?

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:7.hebrew: הא לאי - באמת, על כרחך בריה בידי שמים היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:7.english: Indeed - Truly, perforce it is a creation by the hand of Heaven.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:8.hebrew: יעשנה בדפוס - על ידי יציקה, כמו שיוצקין כלי כסף וכלי נחשת:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:8.english: He can make it in a mold - By means of casting, just as silver vessels and copper vessels are cast.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:7:9.english: And set it at once - All of it at once, quickly.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:9:1.hebrew: ראשית דרכו - קודם לשאר דרכים. והא דאמרן לעיל הכתב בערב שבת — בכתבן של לוחות, וזו היתה כתובה מתחילה באש שחורה על גבי לבנה:
Rashi on Pesachim 54a:9:1.english: The beginning of His way - Before the other ways. And that which we said above, [that] the writing [was created] on Shabbat eve, [refers] to the writing of the Tablets; whereas this [Torah] was written from the beginning with black fire upon white [fire].

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:9:2.english: Before the mountains were brought forth - You created the attribute of repentance.

Rashi on Pesachim 54a:9:3.english: You return man to contrition - Until his heart is crushed before You.

Tosafot on Pesachim 54a:15:1.hebrew: אלה בני שעיר החורי וכו' מלמד שבא צבעון על אמו - תימה, דביש נוחלין (ב"ב קטו:) מוכח מהאי קרא דבני בנים כבנים, וא"כ מנלן שבא על אמו? ועוד, לא מצינו בכל התורה שיקראו לבן אשתו בנו, והכא אמר דלהכי קרי ליה בנו לפי שנולד מאשתו! וי"ל דקרי ליה בנו לפי שהיה בן בנו, כדאמרינן ביש נוחלין, והכא דייק שבא על אמו מדלא כתיב איה, שהיה כמו כן בן צבעון, ולא כתיב אלא ענה לחודיה; ש"מ לפי שהיה נמי בן אשתו של שעיר, כתביה קרא הכא עם שאר בני שעיר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 54a:15:1.english: "These are the sons of Seir the Horite," etc. "This teaches that Zibeon cohabited with his mother" - This is astonishing, for in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 115b) it is proven from this verse that grandchildren are like children, and if so, from where do we know that he cohabited with his mother? And furthermore, we do not find anywhere in the entire Torah that one's wife's son is called his son, yet here [the Gemara] says that for this reason it calls him his son, because he was born from his wife! And one can answer that [Scripture] calls him his son because he was his grandson, as we say in Yesh Nochalin, and here [the Gemara] infers that he cohabited with his mother from the fact that Aiah—who was likewise Zibeon's son—is not written [there], and only Anah alone is written; learn from this that because he was also the son of Seir's wife, Scripture wrote him here with the rest of Seir's sons.
